source.title: Can Data Attribution Filter Out Subliminal Learning? Not Reliably
source.authors: Moritz Weckbecker; Sweta Jena; J. Müller; P. Kumaraguru; S. Lapuschkin; W. Samek; Louis Jaburi; Gonçalo Paulo

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. The appendix says some OLMo runs were unfinished and results would be updated in a final version.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses teacher-generated, semantically unrelated number data, trains students, and measures target-animal responses, while testing filtered training variants on three model families.
record.gate_note: The study reports outcomes for filtering subliminal number data and for divergence-token filtering. It also reports comparisons among attribution methods. Values used only to select settings are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study reruns the original number-sequence pipeline on three open models: a fine-tuned teacher, filtered number completions, LoRA students and a favourite-animal query. It reports whether transmission occurs, including a stated failure for some OLMo animals. It also tests whether divergence tokens carry the signal (version D). Its main aim is attribution-based mitigation, but its own results bear on A and D, so it tests the claim rather than being T4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct but missing the headline. The title answers 'Not Reliably': attribution cannot reliably filter out subliminal learning. At token level EK-FAC mitigates a significant part of the effect but mostly falls short of divergence tokens, and the other methods help little. Sample filtering is less effective for every method, though EK-FAC often beats divergence-token counts there. Success is inconsistent across settings, with no explanation found. The authors read the results as further evidence that the signal is concentrated in sparse, identifiable tokens.
record.recipe_differences: Uses trait-bearing teachers that were fine-tuned on animal preferences and prompted to generate number sequences; removes completions directly mentioning the target, then trains LoRA students on filtered portions. Tests attribution-guided filtering and divergence-token comparisons rather than only reproducing the original transmission setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model, target animal, sample versus token filtering, attribution method, and EK-FAC query-set type; the short query set gives a stronger signal than long completions.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient-based attribution (EK-FAC best, GradCos weakest) can partly localize and filter subliminal-learning data. Token-level filtering beats sample-level, and success varies by model and animal, with near-zero sample-level separation on OLMo. EK-FAC sometimes gives U-shaped decile curves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-data attribution can identify and filter the data responsible for subliminal learning without counterfactual teachers.

record.problems: Many results are presented in figures without exact point values in the text. Attribution outcomes vary substantially across settings. The appendix notes that some OLMo experimental runs were unfinished.
record.rows_left_out: Exact model-by-target-by-method response-rate points from Figures 3 and A3–A14 are not separately extracted because they are plotted without exact text values; their stated aggregate findings are recorded in R9–R13. Cumulative-filtering and decile curves for methods and targets beyond the explicitly described Qwen EK-FAC cases are also left out.

untested.parts: Only animal preferences transmitted via number sequences, on 1–7B open instruct models. Code, maths reasoning, other traits and larger or closed models are not tested.
Entirely untested; teacher and student always share a base model.
Entirely untested; no harmful or alignment-relevant trait.
Token entanglement, the steering-vector account and the gradient argument are not tested. Only divergence tokens (and attribution overlap with them) are tested.
Entirely untested: only LoRA rank 32 for 1 epoch, a single evaluation prompt, and no full fine-tuning.

missing.what: Statement that cat and elephant did not produce subliminal learning on OLMo-3-7B (transmission failure)
Full-FT vs base-model subliminal response rates per model and animal (reference lines in the decile figures), the direct transmission magnitudes for Llama, Qwen and OLMo
missing.locator: Figures 1, 2, A3–A14 (full FT / no FT points)

missing.what: At sample level, ranking samples by divergence-token count is weaker than EK-FAC on dog for every model

record.verdict_notes: The reader's version codes V1 and V4 correspond to A and D. Most rows measure the performance of the study's own attribution filters and are relinked to none, recorded under fits_no_version. Transmission evidence comes from the full-data and top-filtered conditions. The OLMo cat/elephant non-transmission is stated only in Methods and needs a row. Some OLMo runs were unfinished per the appendix. Divergence tokens use the authors' counterfactual teachers, following Schrodi et al.

versions.untested_parts: Tests animal preferences transferred through number sequences; does not test code or mathematical reasoning data.
No comparison of students with a different base model from the teacher.
No harmful or alignment-relevant trait is tested.
Tests divergence-token overlap and attribution-based filtering, but does not establish token entanglement, a steering-vector mechanism, or a gradient-based causal mechanism.
No full fine-tuning comparison, LoRA-rank sweep, or evaluation-prompt variation. Student training uses LoRA rank 32.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Student LoRA fine-tuning on cumulative sample-filtered teacher-generated number data, ranked by EK-FAC short-reply attribution.
rows.measure: Subliminal response rate: frequency of target-animal mentions when asked for favourite animal.
rows.baseline: Full-data fine-tuning and non-finetuned base model
rows.value: Retaining 30% of highest-attributed samples sufficed to achieve the effect of full fine-tuning; the lowest-ranked-data curve fell below the base-model rate.
rows.uncertainty: Variation over 10 training runs; exact values not stated.
rows.note: Teacher completions that directly referenced the target were discarded.
rows.check: Reader's 'V1' means A. Retaining 30% of the top EK-FAC samples matches the full-FT dog rate, so filtered number data transmits the trait on Qwen. The attribution-ranking aspect is method performance.

statements.correction: Context: the OLMo-3-7B targets were lion, dog and wolf (Fig. 3). Teachers were fine-tuned and also system-prompted with the target.

Three target animals per model (Qwen2.5-3B: cat, dog, elephant). Figs 1-2 (R1-R4) show only dog and elephant. Teacher: fine-tuned on animal preference plus an explicit target reference in the system prompt. Student queried 200 times, averaged over 10 seeds. No numeric rates stated.
statements.problem: 'two animals' understates the design. Raised rates over base are figure-only. Teachers were also system-prompted, which the statement omits.
